cards.text: The word of the LORD comes to Joel son of Pethuel, a prophet of God (Acts 2:16). Joel calls out to the elders and to everybody who lives in the land. And he opens with a question that would make anybody put their phone down: "Has anything like this ever happened in your days or in the days of your fathers?"

cards.question: What does Joel tell the elders and everyone in the land to do with what's happened?

answers.text: Pass it down generation after generation
Carve it into the city gate

cards.text: So what's happened? Locusts, and not one kind of locust but FOUR: the devouring locust, the swarming locust, the young locust and the destroying locust.

cards.question: Joel says each kind of locust eats what the kind before it left behind.

cards.text: Then Joel calls out: wake up, you drunkards, and weep, wail, all you drinkers of wine. That is NOT the alarm anybody wants to wake up to.

cards.question: Why does Joel tell the drinkers of wine to wail?

answers.text: The sweet wine is cut off from them
Their wine jars have been smashed
The king has banned all their feasts

cards.text: Then the picture changes: a nation has invaded "My land," powerful and without number, with the teeth of a lion and the fangs of a lioness. WITHOUT NUMBER, friend, like the unread emails of somebody who swears they're "getting to it."

cards.question: This invading nation lays waste the grapevine and goes after the fig tree too. What does it do to the fig tree?

cards.text: It strips off the bark and throws it away, and the branches have turned white. Then Joel says to wail like a virgin dressed in sackcloth, grieving for the husband of her youth.

cards.question: Then Joel says the ___ and drink offerings have been cut off from the house of the LORD.
The priests who minister before the LORD are rejoicing.

cards.text: The field is ruined and the land mourns, because the grain is destroyed, the new wine is dried up and the oil fails. I lose it when a batch comes out one minute late, friend, and these folks just lost the WHOLE field.

cards.question: Joel calls on two groups to be dismayed and wail over the wheat and barley. Who are they?

cards.text: The whole harvest of the field has perished, and then Joel walks us through the orchard: the grapevine, the fig, the pomegranate, the palm, the apple. Every single tree, friend, WITHERED.

cards.question: With every tree in the orchard withered, Joel says surely the ___ of mankind has dried up.

cards.text: Now Joel turns to the priests, the ministers of the altar. Put on sackcloth, he tells them, and lament.

cards.question: Joel tells the priests to put on sackcloth. How long does he tell them to stay in it?

cards.text: Sackcloth, all night long, because the grain and drink offerings are withheld from the house of their God. And I thought sleeping under old takeout menus in a junk drawer was rough.
Then Joel calls for a fast that's set apart, and a solemn assembly. This is the meeting you do NOT skip.

cards.question: Joel says to gather the ___ and all the residents of the land to the house of the LORD.
Once everyone is gathered at the house of the LORD, what does Joel tell them to do?

cards.text: Then Joel cries out, "Alas for the day!" He's talking about the Day of the LORD.

cards.question: Joel says the Day of the LORD is still far off.
Joel says the Day of the LORD will come as ___ from the Almighty.

cards.text: Then Joel asks: hasn't the food been cut off right before our very eyes, and joy and gladness from the house of our God? Not somewhere far away, friend, RIGHT in front of them.
The seeds lie shriveled under the clods, and the storehouses are in ruins. Friend, that's no new batch AND no backup batch.

cards.question: The granaries are broken down too. Why?

answers.text: A flood has washed them out

cards.text: And it's not just the people. The cattle groan, and the herds wander in confusion, like everybody in a parking garage trying to remember where they parked.

cards.question: Why do the herds wander in confusion?

cards.text: Even the flocks of sheep are suffering. Then the words turn to the LORD Himself: "To You, O LORD, I call…"

cards.question: This prayer tells the LORD what has struck the open pastures and the trees of the field. What is it?
The prayer to the LORD says some creatures pant for Him too. Which ones?

cards.text: Why are they panting? The streams of water have dried up and fire has consumed the open pastures, so the one praying and the beasts of the field end up in the same place, friend, reaching out to the LORD.
